mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly relates atoms to elements?

options.A: An element consists of only one kind of atom.
options.B: An element consists of many different atoms.
options.D: Elements are made of molecules only.

mcqs.answer: An element consists of only one kind of atom.
mcqs.explanation: Dalton’s atomic theory states that each element is made up of identical atoms of that element. Therefore, an element is defined by a single type of atom. Option B is wrong because an element does not contain different atoms; that describes a compound. Option C confuses size, and Option D ignores the atomic nature of elements.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand atoms combine to form compounds
mcqs.question: If two atoms of hydrogen combine with one atom of oxygen, which compound is formed?
mcqs.explanation: Dalton’s theory introduced the idea that atoms combine in fixed whole-number ratios. Two hydrogen atoms (2 H) together with one oxygen atom (1 O) give the compound water, whose formula is H₂O. Option B (hydrogen peroxide) needs two oxygen atoms, C is not a stable compound, and D lacks oxygen.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the historical importance of atomic theory
mcqs.question: How did Dalton’s atomic theory differ from the ancient Greek concept of indivisible atoms?

options.A: Dalton proposed that atoms of the same element are identical in mass, whereas Greeks had no such quantitative idea.
options.B: Greeks believed atoms could be created and destroyed, while Dalton said they are indestructible.
options.C: Dalton suggested atoms are divisible, whereas Greeks said they are indivisible.
options.D: Both theories were identical in all respects.

mcqs.answer: Dalton proposed that atoms of the same element are identical in mass, whereas Greeks had no such quantitative idea.
mcqs.explanation: The Greeks (Democritus, Leucippus) introduced the notion of indivisible atoms but did not assign measurable properties such as mass or identicality to atoms of a given element. Dalton, in the 19th century, gave a quantitative description, stating that atoms of a particular element are identical in mass and size. Options B, C, and D misrepresent both the Greek and Daltonian views.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise limitations of the original model
mcqs.question: Which experimental observation could NOT be explained by Dalton’s original atomic theory?
mcqs.explanation: Dalton’s model assumed that all atoms of an element are identical in mass. The discovery of isotopes—atoms of the same element with different masses—contradicts this assumption and therefore could not be explained by his original theory. The other three options (conservation of mass, fixed composition, definite proportions) are all accounted for in Dalton’s postulates.
